BLOCK — performance/292, exactd398803f7169ef29f136704536205e8c8210ae06, base27076a3793d62b8408b0a14aba89a569a710ad47. Answers01a1f8fb-0cf1-7b21-88a4-dc6916a11ce5. Static source review; no builds/tests, benchmark, isolated server, live measurements or daemon changes by this seat.

P292-001 — the required every-path exit bound is not implemented. Live::leave locks Waiters and performs blocking ChildStdin.write_all/flush BEFORE receiver.recv_timeout(TEARDOWN_WAIT). A full pipe/non-reading client can stall before the one-second wait even starts [INFERENCE from blocking I/O semantics; not reproduced by performance]. Drop's subsequent child.wait also has no deadline; ControlClient::release acquires its state mutex, and daemon.shutdown awaits spawn_blocking release without an outer deadline. The constant proves a reply-wait bound, NOT a whole-exit bound.

The new unanswered teardown test starts cat with output discarded. Cat drains stdin, so it proves the lost-reply case while bypassing pipe backpressure; the closed-reader test proves a fast skip. Neither supports the docs' claim that a frozen server cannot hold exit. Required: bound the newly added write/admission as well as reply waiting, and prove the full-pipe/nonreading exit path; distinguish any inherited lock/reap ceiling instead of claiming recv_timeout covers it. Reviewer raven and coder notified and own exact-path runtime/mutation proof.

P292-002 — bounce time/cost qualification. New justfile736 uses bare sleep in a repeated path: up to150 external sleep processes, nominal5 launches/s for one waiting bounce. Repository resource rule requires an absolute repeated launch; use /bin/sleep. The loop is bounded by iteration count, not elapsed time:30 seconds is its nominal requested sleep total, plus spawn/scheduling/kill-probe overhead, not a strict wall-time cap. Qualify or enforce the advertised elapsed bound. kill probes/increment are shell builtins; this is bounce-only work, not per-seat or at-rest load.

| Path | Static rate/cost |
| --- | --- |
| Teardown command | One fixed if-shell -F command over that live client's existing pipe per exit, selecting in-server kill-session or set-option. No new shell/process launch. Per-exit quoting/formatting/channel/queue allocations; no per-read cost added. |
| Reply wait | At most1s AFTER successful write; closed/poisoned reader state skips or failed write skips reply waiting. Entire exit not bounded as above. |
| Replacement | Same exit work also occurs when a read times out/replaces a client; can add up to1s reply-wait latency and unknown blocking-write delay to that read's fallback, not only daemon bounce. |
| Graceful SIGTERM | Additional one-time signal registration and existing event select branch, no periodic loop/timer. Shutdown adds one spawn_blocking release task after workers stop; no OS subprocess at that call. |
| Bounce availability | Release build/install happen before stop. Old daemon drains after SIGINT before new starts; fleet reconnect gap can grow by the old stop duration. Up to30s nominal sleeps, then SIGKILL fallback; existing1.5s new-start wait still applies. Sub-second-gap comment is no longer a guarantee. |
| Attach lock | One open per attach, existing metadata/conditionalchmod/try_lock. Real adapters key it beside tmux socket; path/canonicalization/getuid work is adapter setup, not per tick or per seat. Custom executable keeps private state-root path. |

spawn_sites.rs unchanged (empty exact-base diff verified); original tmux.control-client launch recording retained. No new daemon recurring poller or per-tick/per-seat launch. The bounce loop is new, so a blanket no-new-loop/timer/launch statement would be false. release sets a flag preventing another persistent attach; any subsequent read forks, so stopping workers first matters for cost.

The destructive teardown's decision is the fixed alone predicate: only this session's sole client, one window and one pane allows kill-session; otherwise it preserves the session and switches destroy-unattached off. The attach lock is a brake, not retention: it can only delay/refuse a new attach. Security/correctness own branch and rolling-lock compatibility proof. Packet-reported2000-run before/after crash results were not rerun or independently verified here.
